This sample book explains the tool that renders it. Every chapter you read here is also a set of dots on the landing page: each dot is one passage, and dots that sit close together say similar things.
Drop your own books into the books/ folder, rebuild, and the same page turns into a map of your library. Nothing here needs a server to read; only searching by meaning needs one small local process.

A book is a folder named YYYY-MM-DD_slug. Inside it, OUTLINE.md gives the title, the subtitle and the parts, and each chapter is a markdown file named NN-slug.md. The site reads those files where they are. It never copies them, so a fix in a chapter shows up in the site and in any PDF built from the same files.

The parts come from the ## Part … lines in OUTLINE.md, and the chapters inside a part from the ### Chapter N lines under it. A chapter that no part claims still appears, in a group of its own, so nothing goes missing.

A paragraph that holds only an image becomes a figure with its alt text as the caption. Every figure gets the same frame width as the text column, so pictures line up with code blocks and with each other.

At build time scripts/brain.py cuts every chapter into passages of a few hundred characters. A passage never crosses a chapter, and each one remembers its book, its chapter and the section heading it sits under. Code blocks and image lines are left out, because they carry little meaning on their own.
Chapter 2: Vectors on the Neural Engine

Each passage is turned into a vector by EmbeddingGemma through a local embedding server that runs the model on the Apple Neural Engine. The vectors are cached by the passage text, so a rebuild only embeds what changed.
Chapter 2: Vectors on the Neural Engine

The build writes small static files: the 3D positions, the book of every passage, its four nearest neighbours in meaning, the passage texts, and the vectors themselves in two sizes. The 256-dimension copy feeds the map; the full 768-dimension copy feeds search, which ranks better.
Chapter 3: The map and the search
Two layouts from the same vectors

UMAP turns the vectors into a 3D layout. The page offers two views of it. Separate gives each book its own cloud with its cover floating above it. Combined puts every book into one shared space, so books that talk about the same thing land on top of each other, and lines appear between passages of different books that mean nearly the same.
Chapter 3: The map and the search

Clicking a dot opens the passage, lights up its four nearest neighbours and sends light along the paths between them. The explore button walks through the cross-book pairs one by one. Any click hands control back to you.
Chapter 3: The map and the search

With the small local server running, a query is embedded the same way as the passages and compared with every vector. On a plain static host there is no server, so the page falls back to matching exact words. The same prebuilt vectors are also served to AI agents through a local MCP server.
